title: Authentication
description: Authentication system architecture of Rozgar Connect
features: JWT (JSON Web Token) based user session authentication
Dual-token system consisting of a short-lived Access Token and a long-lived Refresh Token
Secure cookie storage for the Refresh Token to prevent client-side XSS access
Axios-based frontend interceptors to manage token attaching and automatic transparent sessions refresh
Route-level role authorization gates based on JWT decoded claims

accessToken.contents: Decoded user ID, name, email, and array of roles
accessToken.usage: Sent in the Authorization header as Bearer token for api requests

refreshToken.usage: Used exclusively to query /api/v1/auth/refresh to fetch a new access token

axios_interceptors.request: Intercepts all outgoing HTTP requests, retrieves the current access token from Redux memory, and sets it in the 'Authorization: Bearer <token>' header if it exists.
axios_interceptors.response: Intercepts incoming responses. If a request fails with a 401 Unauthorized status and is not a login/register/refresh request itself, it triggers a token refresh: 1) If a refresh is already in progress, it queues subsequent requests. 2) Performs a POST request to '/auth/refresh' to obtain a new access token. 3) Stores the new access token in Redux. 4) Retries all queued requests. 5) If refresh fails (token expired/invalid), it clears cookies and logs the user out.

unimplemented_features: Forgot Password is not currently implemented in this version of the application
Reset Password is not currently implemented in this version of the application
notes: The secure flag on cookie options is set to false in development mode to allow local network IP/WiFi testing and cross-device browser operations.
The refresh token is automatically matched against the token saved in the database for that user to ensure session validity and prevent token reuse/replay attacks.
